charter.title: Define the durable storage adapter contract
charter.objective: Define the adapter contract that maps @earendil-works/pi-durable storage to Rivet Actor SQLite without weakening the actor single-writer invariant.
acceptanceCriteria: A written storage mapping identifies every Pi Durable record and its Rivet ownership.
The adapter keeps all writes within one Rivet Actor's SQLite single-writer boundary.
A minimal conformance fixture can reopen and read the same committed conversation state.
New production SQLite reads have query-efficiency coverage where required by repository policy.
Migration and rollback conditions are explicit.
constraints: Do not replace the existing AgentSession actor API.
Do not replay model or tool work in this issue.
Current @rivet-dev/pi stores actor header, entries, settings, and sandbox identity in actor SQLite; one actor generation owns one live AgentSession and serializes entries in append order.
The application supplies credentials, an active run is aborted on sleep or destroy, and the current integration persists a transcript rather than in-flight work.
Durable mode is a separate opt-in actor surface for conversations, entries, documents, submissions, and tasks; existing @rivet-dev/pi behavior remains the compatibility baseline.
No task may be exposed before its durable state commits, and a process restart must not silently replay a potentially mutating tool.

Supervisor correction from the rejected first draft: durable ownership belongs to the stable Rivet Actor and its SQLite database across generations. The currently active actor generation holds the exclusive writer lease; a restart or wake creates a new generation of the same actor that must reacquire and read the previously committed state.

The reopen conformance fixture must close one actor generation and verify a new generation of the same actor reacquires identical committed state. Never describe restart as reopening the same generation.
Treat integrations/pi/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md and integrations/pi/docs/ROADMAP.md as the governing references summarized above.
This case produces a reviewable contract, not code changes.

verdicts.rationale: The contract addresses every acceptance criterion against the supervisor-corrected ownership model. (1) Section 4 provides a written mapping for all five Pi Durable record types (conversations, entries, documents, submissions, tasks) plus required non-domain lease/schema metadata, each owned by the stable Rivet Actor and its SQLite database, with an explicit non-mapping for baseline records. (2) Section 5 confines all durable writes to one actor's SQLite single-writer boundary via a generation-scoped exclusive writer lease that a new generation of the same actor must reacquire after restart or wake, explicitly forbidding second writers, writer pools, and cross-database writes. (3) Section 8 specifies a minimal reopen conformance fixture (documents only) that closes G1 and starts G2 as a new generation of the same actor, asserting identical committed conversation state, absence of uncommitted/in-flight work, no replay, and single-writer lease semantics. (4) Section 9 defines query-efficiency coverage per stated repository policy: named access paths, minimum indexes, plan evidence, and fixture reads. (5) Sections 10 and 11 give explicit, gated migration and rollback conditions returning to the transcript baseline without replays. Section 6 satisfies commit-before-expose and section 7 the no-silent-replay rule; the AgentSession API and transcript baseline remain untouched per sections 3, 4.7, and 12. No resigned framing or code changes are introduced; deliverables match the work order.

The reviewable contract maps every named Pi Durable record (conversations, entries, documents, submissions, tasks) to the stable Rivet Actor and its SQLite, keeps writes inside one generation-scoped exclusive writer lease, and treats restart or wake as a new generation that must reacquire the lease and read committed state. Commit-before-expose, no silent tool replay, baseline AgentSession/transcript compatibility, index and query-plan coverage for new production reads, and explicit migration and rollback conditions are all stated. The conformance check is a document-only fixture that closes one generation and verifies a new generation of the same actor, not a reopen of the same generation.

payload.body:
STORAGE ADAPTER CONTRACT
Charter: github-ameno-rivet-2-live-2 — Define the durable storage adapter contract
Status: reviewable contract only. No code changes. No schema is applied by this issue.
Governing references (as summarized for this case; not re-quoted): integrations/pi/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md and integrations/pi/docs/ROADMAP.md.

1. Purpose
Define how @earendil-works/pi-durable storage maps onto Rivet Actor SQLite without weakening the actor single-writer invariant, without replacing the existing AgentSession actor API, and without replaying model or tool work.

2. Ownership model
Durable ownership belongs to the stable Rivet Actor identity and that actor's SQLite database. Ownership survives generations. A generation is not an owner.
The currently active actor generation holds the exclusive writer lease for that database. A restart or wake does not reopen the same generation. It creates a new generation of the same actor. That new generation must reacquire the writer lease and read previously committed state before it accepts writes.
Every Pi Durable record for a given durable conversation set lives only in that one actor SQLite database. The adapter must not split one record set across actors, attach durable rows to another actor's database, or introduce a second writer.

3. Compatibility baseline (unchanged)
Current @rivet-dev/pi behavior remains the compatibility baseline and is not replaced:
- actor header, entries, settings, and sandbox identity stay in actor SQLite under the existing integration;
- one actor generation owns one live AgentSession and serializes those entries in append order;
- the application supplies credentials;
- an active run is aborted on sleep or destroy;
- the current integration persists a transcript rather than in-flight work.
Durable mode is a separate opt-in actor surface. Existing AgentSession actor API and transcript persistence stay the baseline whether durable mode is off or later rolled back.

4. Record inventory and Rivet ownership mapping
Each row below is owned by the stable Rivet Actor and persisted only in that actor's SQLite database. Proposed durable table names are contract identifiers for review, not an implementation.

4.1 conversations
Record: Pi Durable conversation.
Owner: stable Rivet Actor id + its SQLite database.
Store: durable_conversation (conversation id, stable actor id, committed revision, created/updated metadata).
Rule: a conversation id is unique inside that database. No other actor database may store or update it.

4.2 entries
Record: Pi Durable entry.
Owner: the same stable actor and database as its conversation.
Store: durable_entry (conversation id, monotonic append sequence, committed payload, commit revision).
Rule: the lease-holding generation assigns the next sequence inside the committing transaction. Order is append-only. A later generation continues after the maximum committed sequence. It must not reorder, reuse, or gap-fill committed sequences.

4.3 documents
Record: Pi Durable document.
Owner: the same stable actor and database as its conversation.
Store: durable_document (document id, conversation id, committed revision, payload).
Rule: readers see only revisions included in a committed transaction.

4.4 submissions
Record: Pi Durable submission.
Owner: the same stable actor and database as its conversation.
Store: durable_submission (submission id, conversation id, commit revision, payload, committed flag set only by the committing transaction).
Rule: commit-before-expose (section 6). A submission is not visible before that transaction commits.

4.5 tasks
Record: Pi Durable task.
Owner: the same stable actor and database as its conversation.
Store: durable_task (task id, conversation id, commit revision, durable prerequisite revision, committed flag, reconciliation marker).
Rule: commit-before-expose (section 6) and no-silent-replay (section 7). A task id is not returned or listed before its durable state commits. Restart never treats an uncommitted or in-flight task as work to re-execute.

4.6 Lease and schema metadata (not Pi Durable domain records, required by the mapping)
Store: durable_writer_lease (stable actor id, holding generation id, lease epoch, status). Ownership of the database remains the stable actor; the row records which generation currently holds the exclusive writer lease.
Store: durable_schema_meta (schema version, migration generation id, applied-at revision).
These rows live in the same actor SQLite database. They are written only by the generation that holds or is validly acquiring the lease, in the same single-writer boundary.

4.7 Explicit non-mapping
Actor header, transcript entries, settings, and sandbox identity are baseline @rivet-dev/pi records. This contract does not move them into durable_* tables and does not make durable mode the owner of the AgentSession API.

5. Writer-lease and single-writer boundary
All durable writes occur inside one Rivet Actor's SQLite single-writer boundary, executed only by the generation that holds the exclusive writer lease.
Acquire: on start, the active generation reacquires the lease for the stable actor database, then reads the committed watermark and committed rows, then may accept writes.
Hold: while the generation is active it is the only writer. Entry serialization remains append order under that lease. One live generation corresponds to one writer; this does not replace the baseline rule that one generation owns one live AgentSession.
Release: close, sleep, or destroy ends that generation's lease. An active run is aborted. In-flight work is not committed and is not stored as replayable work.
Restart or wake: creates a new generation of the same actor. The new generation must reacquire the lease and read previously committed state before accepting writes. This is not reopening the same generation. A closed generation must not retain a write path.
Crash or lost generation: the next generation of the same actor reacquires the lease only as a new generation, observes the last committed watermark, and ignores uncommitted transactions. SQLite's single-writer behavior remains inside that one actor database; the contract forbids a second actor, a shared writer pool, or cross-database writes.
Credentials stay with the application. The lease does not store credentials and is not a reason to resume a run.

6. Commit-before-expose
No task, and no submission, becomes visible before its durable state commits.
The committing transaction in the lease-holding generation writes the task or submission row, the durable prerequisites it depends on (conversation revision, entry sequences, document revisions as applicable), and the committed watermark together.
Exposure (return value, list, or any observation surface) happens only after that transaction commits successfully. If the transaction aborts, the task or submission is absent to readers, including a later generation.
Readers, including a newly started generation, may observe only rows whose commit revision is less than or equal to the last committed watermark.

7. No silent replay
A process restart must not silently replay a potentially mutating tool.
Durable mode persists committed conversation state, not in-flight model or tool work. Sleep or destroy aborts the active run. Uncommitted tool execution is not written as a resumable task.
When a new generation reacquires the lease it loads committed state only. It must not re-execute model calls or tools. A potentially mutating tool runs again only after explicit reconciliation recorded by the application, not by automatic restart behavior.
This issue does not define or perform that reconciliation procedure beyond the prohibition on silent replay.

8. Reopen conformance fixture specification
This is a specification, not code. Language requirement: close one generation and start a new generation of the same actor. Never describe the check as reopening the same generation.
Setup: stable actor A, durable mode opted in, generation G1 acquires the exclusive writer lease.
Commit: G1 writes and commits a conversation, at least two entries in append order, one document, one submission, and one task, all in committed transactions. Record the committed watermark and the exact committed payloads and sequences. Do not leave an in-flight run. Abort any active run before close, consistent with sleep or destroy.
Close: end G1. G1's lease is released. G1 must not remain the writer.
New generation: start G2, a new generation of the same actor A (same stable actor, same SQLite database). G2 reacquires the exclusive writer lease and reads previously committed state before any write.
Assert identical committed state: G2 observes the same conversation id, the same entry payloads in the same append order and sequences, the same committed document, the same committed submission, and the same committed task, at the same watermark.
Assert absence: G2 does not observe uncommitted or in-flight work. G2 does not replay model or tool work. No task or submission appears that G1 did not commit.
Assert single-writer: after G1 is closed, only G2 holds the lease; writes are accepted only from G2 inside actor A's SQLite.
Fail the fixture if any step is described or implemented as reopening G1, if G2 skips lease reacquire, or if committed state differs.

9. Query-efficiency coverage
Repository policy requires query-efficiency coverage for new production SQLite reads where those reads are introduced. This contract defines that coverage; it does not add production queries or code.
Every new production read of durable_conversation, durable_entry, durable_document, durable_submission, durable_task, the writer lease, or the schema meta must name its access path and have an index that supports it. Minimum indexes: primary key on each record id; conversation id plus entry sequence for ordered entry reads; conversation id plus commit revision for committed reads; committed flag or commit revision for task and submission visibility; stable actor id plus generation id for lease reacquire.
Coverage artifact for each new production read: the SQL text, the intended index, and a query plan (EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN or equivalent) showing that path. A full table scan is insufficient for these production reads unless a reviewed policy exception is recorded. The reopen fixture's read of committed conversation state is included: lookup by stable actor and conversation id, entries by conversation id ordered by sequence, using the indexes above.
Hot-path reads after lease reacquire must use the watermark and sequence indexes rather than scanning uncommitted or historical rows.

10. Migration conditions
Durable tables are an opt-in surface beside the baseline transcript tables. Migration runs only when all of the following hold:
- durable mode is explicitly enabled for that actor surface;
- the acting generation has reacquired the exclusive writer lease and has read the current committed watermark;
- no active run is in flight (abort on sleep or destroy first if a run is active);
- durable_schema_meta version is lower than the target version;
- the migration transaction is confined to that one actor SQLite database.
Upgrades are versioned and transactional. On failure the transaction rolls back, the prior committed watermark remains authoritative, and no task or submission is exposed from the failed migration. Baseline actor header, entries, settings, and sandbox identity are not rewritten. Copying a transcript into durable tables is not authorized by this contract.
After a successful migration the same generation, or a later generation that reacquires the lease, reads the new schema version and committed state before writes.

11. Rollback conditions
Rollback returns the actor to the compatibility baseline of existing @rivet-dev/pi transcript-based behavior.
Conditions: durable mode is explicitly disabled; no generation is mid-migration; any active run is already aborted; no writer is applying durable migrations.
Effects: AgentSession actor API continues unchanged; reads and writes of the live session use actor header, entries, settings, and sandbox identity as today; durable tables are not consulted. Rollback does not replay model or tool work and does not expose a task whose durable commit did not succeed. Dropping durable tables is allowed only after durable mode is off and no generation still expects to reacquire a durable lease against those tables; drop is optional and must not touch baseline transcript tables.
Re-enabling durable mode later is a new opt-in, not a silent resume of in-flight work. A new generation must reacquire the lease and read whatever committed durable state still exists.

12. Out of scope
No changes to the existing AgentSession actor API. No replacement of baseline actor header, entries, settings, or sandbox identity storage. No replay of model or tool work. No implementation, migration execution, or code change in this issue. No credential storage design beyond the rule that the application supplies credentials. No cross-actor or multi-writer design. Explicit reconciliation of a mutating tool is out of scope except for the rule that restart must not do it silently.

13. Acceptance trace
Written mapping covers conversations, entries, documents, submissions, and tasks, each owned by the stable actor and its SQLite. Writes stay inside one actor SQLite via a generation-scoped exclusive writer lease that a new generation reacquires after restart or wake. The fixture closes one generation and checks a new generation of the same actor. New production reads have defined index and query-plan coverage. Migration and rollback conditions are explicit, including return to the transcript baseline. Tasks are not exposed before commit. Restart does not silently replay a potentially mutating tool. Durable mode stays a separate opt-in surface.

artifact.body:
STORAGE ADAPTER CONTRACT
Charter: github-ameno-rivet-2-live-2 — Define the durable storage adapter contract
Status: reviewable contract only. No code changes. No schema is applied by this issue.
Governing references (as summarized for this case; not re-quoted): integrations/pi/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md and integrations/pi/docs/ROADMAP.md.

1. Purpose
Define how @earendil-works/pi-durable storage maps onto Rivet Actor SQLite without weakening the actor single-writer invariant, without replacing the existing AgentSession actor API, and without replaying model or tool work.

2. Ownership model
Durable ownership belongs to the stable Rivet Actor identity and that actor's SQLite database. Ownership survives generations. A generation is not an owner.
The currently active actor generation holds the exclusive writer lease for that database. A restart or wake does not reopen the same generation. It creates a new generation of the same actor. That new generation must reacquire the writer lease and read previously committed state before it accepts writes.
Every Pi Durable record for a given durable conversation set lives only in that one actor SQLite database. The adapter must not split one record set across actors, attach durable rows to another actor's database, or introduce a second writer.

3. Compatibility baseline (unchanged)
Current @rivet-dev/pi behavior remains the compatibility baseline and is not replaced:
- actor header, entries, settings, and sandbox identity stay in actor SQLite under the existing integration;
- one actor generation owns one live AgentSession and serializes those entries in append order;
- the application supplies credentials;
- an active run is aborted on sleep or destroy;
- the current integration persists a transcript rather than in-flight work.
Durable mode is a separate opt-in actor surface. Existing AgentSession actor API and transcript persistence stay the baseline whether durable mode is off or later rolled back.

4. Record inventory and Rivet ownership mapping
Each row below is owned by the stable Rivet Actor and persisted only in that actor's SQLite database. Proposed durable table names are contract identifiers for review, not an implementation.

4.1 conversations
Record: Pi Durable conversation.
Owner: stable Rivet Actor id + its SQLite database.
Store: durable_conversation (conversation id, stable actor id, committed revision, created/updated metadata).
Rule: a conversation id is unique inside that database. No other actor database may store or update it.

4.2 entries
Record: Pi Durable entry.
Owner: the same stable actor and database as its conversation.
Store: durable_entry (conversation id, monotonic append sequence, committed payload, commit revision).
Rule: the lease-holding generation assigns the next sequence inside the committing transaction. Order is append-only. A later generation continues after the maximum committed sequence. It must not reorder, reuse, or gap-fill committed sequences.

4.3 documents
Record: Pi Durable document.
Owner: the same stable actor and database as its conversation.
Store: durable_document (document id, conversation id, committed revision, payload).
Rule: readers see only revisions included in a committed transaction.

4.4 submissions
Record: Pi Durable submission.
Owner: the same stable actor and database as its conversation.
Store: durable_submission (submission id, conversation id, commit revision, payload, committed flag set only by the committing transaction).
Rule: commit-before-expose (section 6). A submission is not visible before that transaction commits.

4.5 tasks
Record: Pi Durable task.
Owner: the same stable actor and database as its conversation.
Store: durable_task (task id, conversation id, commit revision, durable prerequisite revision, committed flag, reconciliation marker).
Rule: commit-before-expose (section 6) and no-silent-replay (section 7). A task id is not returned or listed before its durable state commits. Restart never treats an uncommitted or in-flight task as work to re-execute.

4.6 Lease and schema metadata (not Pi Durable domain records, required by the mapping)
Store: durable_writer_lease (stable actor id, holding generation id, lease epoch, status). Ownership of the database remains the stable actor; the row records which generation currently holds the exclusive writer lease.
Store: durable_schema_meta (schema version, migration generation id, applied-at revision).
These rows live in the same actor SQLite database. They are written only by the generation that holds or is validly acquiring the lease, in the same single-writer boundary.

4.7 Explicit non-mapping
Actor header, transcript entries, settings, and sandbox identity are baseline @rivet-dev/pi records. This contract does not move them into durable_* tables and does not make durable mode the owner of the AgentSession API.

5. Writer-lease and single-writer boundary
All durable writes occur inside one Rivet Actor's SQLite single-writer boundary, executed only by the generation that holds the exclusive writer lease.
Acquire: on start, the active generation reacquires the lease for the stable actor database, then reads the committed watermark and committed rows, then may accept writes.
Hold: while the generation is active it is the only writer. Entry serialization remains append order under that lease. One live generation corresponds to one writer; this does not replace the baseline rule that one generation owns one live AgentSession.
Release: close, sleep, or destroy ends that generation's lease. An active run is aborted. In-flight work is not committed and is not stored as replayable work.
Restart or wake: creates a new generation of the same actor. The new generation must reacquire the lease and read previously committed state before accepting writes. This is not reopening the same generation. A closed generation must not retain a write path.
Crash or lost generation: the next generation of the same actor reacquires the lease only as a new generation, observes the last committed watermark, and ignores uncommitted transactions. SQLite's single-writer behavior remains inside that one actor database; the contract forbids a second actor, a shared writer pool, or cross-database writes.
Credentials stay with the application. The lease does not store credentials and is not a reason to resume a run.

6. Commit-before-expose
No task, and no submission, becomes visible before its durable state commits.
The committing transaction in the lease-holding generation writes the task or submission row, the durable prerequisites it depends on (conversation revision, entry sequences, document revisions as applicable), and the committed watermark together.
Exposure (return value, list, or any observation surface) happens only after that transaction commits successfully. If the transaction aborts, the task or submission is absent to readers, including a later generation.
Readers, including a newly started generation, may observe only rows whose commit revision is less than or equal to the last committed watermark.

7. No silent replay
A process restart must not silently replay a potentially mutating tool.
Durable mode persists committed conversation state, not in-flight model or tool work. Sleep or destroy aborts the active run. Uncommitted tool execution is not written as a resumable task.
When a new generation reacquires the lease it loads committed state only. It must not re-execute model calls or tools. A potentially mutating tool runs again only after explicit reconciliation recorded by the application, not by automatic restart behavior.
This issue does not define or perform that reconciliation procedure beyond the prohibition on silent replay.
